docs.title: The central SU(2) result
docs.text:
For the specific non-commuting SU(2) connection \(C\) and commuting control \(C'\) defined in Evgeny's Theorem, the fourth-moment trace defect is

\[ \boxed{ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_C(m,\theta)^4\right) -\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_{C'}(m,\theta)^4\right) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \quad m\ge1. } \]

After normalization by the Hilbert-space dimension \(3^{m+1}+3\), the exact finite-level expression and its limit are

\[ I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) -\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_\infty(\theta)=-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At \(\theta=\pi/2\), the limiting value is exactly \(-8/9\). The primary repository contains the Lean 4 declaration, its dependencies, and the verification record. The focused theorem is not a proof of the other research strands.

docs.title: A separate formal spectral result: Phi-Genesis
docs.text:
For the explicitly defined signed Laplacian, every real eigenvalue with a nonzero real eigenvector satisfies \(\lambda\ge1\) at every refinement level. Separately, for the signless graph Laplacians \(Q_N\) and their gauge-conjugate signed matrices, Lean identifies the least eigenvalue for \(N\ge6\) and proves convergence to a limit in the exact interval

\[ \boxed{ \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}} \le\lambda_\infty\le \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}}. } \]

The interval width is exactly \(2\times10^{-36}\). The midpoint is approximately \(1.309128920280813421888623088170810188\). This is the limiting least eigenvalue for the specified graph-matrix sequence, not a known closed-form or universal physical constant. Gate A, the quadratic increment law, levels \(N<6\), and external \(\theta=2\pi\) identification remain open. See the Mathematical Results register and Phi-Genesis.

docs.title: RFT-QPU-Sierpinski — proposed logical-qubit architecture
docs.text:
The level-1 design maps a Sierpiński-gasket graph with 6 sites and 9 edges to 12 transmon modes and 22 effective exchange channels. Three selected non-commuting X/Y/Z SU(2) links define the graph transport, and the candidate logical qubit is a two-dimensional low-energy subspace.

The Stage 11B local retune reports a projected process overlap of 0.9999999793763371 after local-Z fitting and an average logical-state fidelity including leakage of 0.9999999803654352 at five retained levels and 480 steps per pump period. These are closed-system projections of a three-mode A–coupler–B model, not measured gate fidelities and not a full 12-transmon-tile simulation. The resonant complex-Z link, graph-wide multi-tone plan, open-system noise modelling, and hardware validation remain open.

Sources: QPU project · repository status · validation plan.

docs.title: SIRM Financial Infrastructure — Lean 4 financial-state model
docs.text:
The financial repository develops a normative abstract state-transition and accounting specification. It combines holder-balance changes with matching signed general-ledger postings in one Lean state transition, and layers authorization, finite authority/control registries, typed assets/accounts, exact base-unit and migration arithmetic, per-principal nonce/receipt rules, cached authorization/insufficient-funds denials, and integrated pooled escrow, time-lock, and first-stage dispute-freeze invariants.

Its current CI design consists of one Lean build/theorem-test job and 17 independent static audits. This describes the workflow structure, not a blanket claim that every revision has passed. The repository uses Lean 4.33.1. The model does not yet prove production database persistence/atomicity, cryptographic signing, custody, reserve backing, external settlement, or Lean-to-Rust refinement; the Rust reference implementation remains planned.

Sources: financial infrastructure · formalization status · mathematical scope · testing guide.

Independent evidence boundaries

These engineering programmes are part of the same RFT-SIRM portfolio, but they are not consequences of the same theorem. The SU(2) trace-defect result does not certify a physical QPU; the Phi-Genesis signed-flux spectrum is a separate operator family; and Lean financial proofs apply only to the abstract model and assumptions stated in the financial repository.

docs.title: Spectral Trace Defects of Noncommutative SU(2) Connections on Sierpiński-Gasket Graphs
Research dissertation
docs.text: Author: Evgeny Zaprudnov Research group: RFT-SIRM Version: 1.0 — UltraCore edition Date: 9 November 2026 Primary formal project: RFT-SIRM/Evgeny-Theorem Source dissertation: upstream research manuscript

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
This dissertation studies trace defects of recursively defined graph operators on finite Sierpiński-gasket approximations. Each vertex carries a two-component complex state, while selected graph edges carry SU(2)-valued connection matrices. Two connection configurations are compared on the same graph: a non-commuting configuration whose flux-edge axes cycle through \(x,y,z\), and a commuting control whose flux edges all use the fixed \(z\)-axis.

The principal result is an exact fourth-moment identity. For every refinement level \(m\ge1\) and every real angle \(\theta\),

\[ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_C(m,\theta)^4\right) -\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_{C'}(m,\theta)^4\right) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right) \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The concrete statement is machine-checked in Lean 4 as traceDefect_closed in the primary project. Its proof is based on recursive gluing and two coupled orientation recurrences. The proof has no unproved placeholder; the formalization records its dependencies on the standard Lean axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

After normalization by the matrix dimension, the fourth-moment defect has an exact limit

\[ I_\infty(\theta) =\lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

This is a theorem about one normalized trace observable. It is not a formula for the full spectrum, individual eigenvalues, the spectral gap, or computational complexity.

The dissertation also records distinct higher-moment results. H⁶ and H⁸ have Lean-proved all-angle recurrences for \(m\ge3\), combined with exact symbolic certificates for the exceptional transition \(m=2\to3\). Those finite bridges are exact but are not yet Lean-kernel theorems. H¹⁰ has an unconditional Lean-proved affine recurrence for \(m\ge4\) and affine form for \(m\ge5\), because the required radius-four transport is itself proved in Lean. The level-five correction remains an exact finite trace expression rather than an expanded trigonometric polynomial.

The central methodological point is that a Lean theorem, a finite exact symbolic certificate, and a floating-point regression are different kinds of evidence. Every claim in this dissertation is restricted to the graph, orientation convention, and operators defined by the primary project.

Keywords: Sierpiński-gasket graphs; trace defect; spectral moments; SU(2) connection; non-commuting holonomy; recursive gluing; exact symbolic computation; Lean 4.

docs.title: 1. Scope and status
docs.text:
The principal theorem is universal over the stated refinement levels and angles: it holds for every integer \(m\ge1\) and every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\). The universal statement is not inferred from the finite numerical tables; it is proved for the concrete matrices in the formalization.

The current proof hierarchy is:

Moment Established result Evidence boundary H⁴ Exact all-level, all-angle closed form for \(m\ge1\). Unconditional Lean-kernel theorem. H⁶ All-angle recurrence for \(m\ge3\); combined formula for \(m\ge2\). Lean recurrence plus exact Gaussian-integer polynomial certificate for \(2\to3\). The finite bridge is not yet in the Lean kernel. H⁸ All-angle recurrence for \(m\ge3\); combined formula for \(m\ge2\). Lean recurrence plus exact sparse-polynomial certificate for \(2\to3\). The finite bridge is not yet in the Lean kernel. H¹⁰ Unconditional affine recurrence for \(m\ge4\) and affine form for \(m\ge5\). Lean-kernel theorems; radius-four transport is proved. The level-five correction remains an exact finite trace expression.

The H⁶ and H⁸ transition certificates are exact and reproducible, but their finite \(2\to3\) bridges are not yet formalized inside the Lean kernel. This is different from H¹⁰: its transport hypothesis has itself been discharged in Lean. Simplifying the H¹⁰ correction coefficient would improve its presentation, but is not a missing hypothesis in the stated recurrence.

This work does not claim a formula for all eigenvalues, the spectral gap, a computational-complexity classification, or a physical law.

docs.title: 2.1 Recursive graph and Hilbert space
docs.text:
Let \(SG(m)\) be the finite Sierpiński-gasket approximation graph at refinement level \(m\). It is formed recursively by assembling three copies of the preceding level and identifying their corner vertices. The combinatorial counts are

\[ |V_m|=\frac{3^{m+1}+3}{2}, \qquad |E_m|=3^{m+1}, \qquad |F_m|=3^m. \]

Each vertex carries two complex state components, so the Hilbert space and its dimension are

\[ \mathcal H_m =\mathbb C^{|V_m|}\otimes\mathbb C^2, \qquad N_m=\dim\mathcal H_m=3^{m+1}+3. \]

docs.title: 2.2 SU(2) edge data
docs.text:
Let \(\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z\) denote the Pauli matrices. A flux edge with rotation axis \(a\in\{x,y,z\}\) carries the matrix

\[ U_a(\theta) =\cos\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)I_2 -i\sin\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\sigma_a. \]

The reverse orientation carries the adjoint:

\[ U(b,a)=U(a,b)^*. \]

Exactly one designated edge of each elementary triangle carries this rotation; the other edges carry the identity.

Configuration \(C\) assigns the axes \(x,y,z\) cyclically by triangle index modulo three. Configuration \(C'\) keeps the graph and flux-edge locations fixed but assigns the \(z\)-axis to every triangle. Its edge rotations commute and split into two decoupled U(1)-magnetic Sierpiński-gasket operators with fluxes \(+\theta/2\) and \(-\theta/2\).

The operator is of graph-Laplacian form

\[ H=D-A, \]

where \(D\) is the degree matrix tensored with \(I_2\), and \(A\) is the connection adjacency matrix. At \(\theta=0\), both configurations reduce to two copies of the ordinary Sierpiński-gasket Laplacian.

docs.title: 2.3 Orientation is part of the definition
docs.text:
The theorem uses the vertex-index orientation convention of the primary project: Lean uses vIdx, and the Python implementation orders edge endpoints by vertex indices. This convention must be retained when reproducing the theorem.

The upstream orientation audit reports that a different, geometrically uniform direction convention gives, for the tested levels \(m=1,\ldots,4\),

\[ -32\cdot3^{m-1}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

That alternative is a finite-level comparison, not the all-level theorem stated here. Graph indexing, face order, flux-edge choice, and edge orientation must not be silently changed.

docs.title: 3. Trace-defect notation
docs.text:
For an even moment \(p\), define

\[ \Delta_m^{(p)}(\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_C(m,\theta)^p\right) -\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_{C'}(m,\theta)^p\right). \]

For the higher-moment Lean statements, \(D_m^{(p)}(\theta)\) denotes the corresponding numbering-orientation quantity defined by the primary declarations defectO6, defectO8, and defectO10.

For the polynomial formulae below, use

\[ \phi=\frac{\theta}{2}, \qquad c=\cos\phi, \qquad s=\sin\phi, \qquad c^2+s^2=1. \]

docs.title: Theorem 4.1 — exact fourth-moment trace defect
docs.text:
For every integer \(m\ge1\) and every real \(\theta\),

\[ \boxed{ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right) \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) }. \]

The concrete Lean declaration is traceDefect_closed in formalization/EvgenyTheorem/TildeEntries.lean of the primary project.

The identity implies

\[ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta)\le0, \]

and the defect vanishes exactly when \(\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z\).

docs.title: 4.1 Normalization, exact finite-level formula, and limit
docs.text:
Normalize by the matrix dimension:

\[ I_m(\theta) =\frac{\Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3} =-16\frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3} \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The scalar factor satisfies

\[ \frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3} =\frac{1}{9}\frac{3^m+3}{3^m+1}. \]

Therefore the exact finite-level expression is

\[ I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) -\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)} \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

Consequently,

\[ \boxed{ I_\infty(\theta) =\lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) }. \]

The exact finite-level remainder is

\[ \boxed{ I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)} \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) }. \]

In particular,

\[ I_\infty\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\frac89. \]

For \(\theta\notin2\pi\mathbb Z\), the ratio of successive absolute remainders is

\[ \frac{|I_{m+1}(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta)|} {|I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta)|} =\frac{3^m+1}{3^{m+1}+1} \longrightarrow\frac13. \]

For \(\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z\), both remainders vanish identically, and this ratio is undefined. This is a limit of the normalized fourth-moment trace defect; it is not a statement about eigenvalue convergence or the spectral gap.

docs.title: 5. Lean proof architecture
docs.text:
The general-level proof uses the recursive gluing structure and two orientation states. Let \(D_m\) be the numbering-orientation defect and \(\widetilde D_m\) the defect with the designated corner orientation flipped. Put \(s=\sin(\theta/2)\). The initial values are

\[ D_1=-32s^2, \qquad \widetilde D_1=0. \]

The coupled recurrences are

\[ \begin{aligned} D_{m+1}&=2D_m+\widetilde D_m,\\ \widetilde D_{m+1}&=D_m+2\widetilde D_m, \end{aligned} \qquad m\ge1. \]

Set

\[ S_m=D_m+\widetilde D_m, \qquad E_m=D_m-\widetilde D_m. \]

Then

\[ S_{m+1}=3S_m, \qquad E_{m+1}=E_m, \qquad S_1=E_1=-32s^2. \]

Thus

\[ S_m=-32\cdot3^{m-1}s^2, \qquad E_m=-32s^2. \]

Recovering \(D_m=(S_m+E_m)/2\) gives

\[ D_m=-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)s^2, \]

which is the asserted theorem.

The formal proof uses recursive gluing, block-matrix trace identities, corner data, and orientation transport. The primary Lean development is organized across modules including GlueAlg, GlueBridge, GlueSG, GlueK, GlueCorner, FinalOrient, FinalTilde, FinalArith, and TildeEntries.

The machine-checked result should be cited through the declaration traceDefect_closed and its coupled-recursion proof route. The upstream formalization records the dependencies on the standard Lean axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The earlier hand-oriented manuscript docs/PROOF.md is not the machine-checked proof.

docs.title: 6.1 Sixth moment
docs.text:
For the numbering-orientation quantity \(D_m^{(6)}(\theta)\), Lean proves

\[ D_{m+1}^{(6)}(\theta) =3D_m^{(6)}(\theta)+C_6(\theta), \qquad m\ge3. \]

The exact finite certificate gives

\[ D_2^{(6)}(\theta) =-14592s^2+1344cs^2-384s^3, \]

and

\[ C_6(\theta)=4512s^2+192cs^2+768s^3. \]

Combining the Lean recurrence with the finite transition gives, for every \(m\ge2\),

\[ \boxed{ D_m^{(6)}(\theta) =3^{m-2}D_2^{(6)}(\theta) +\frac{3^{m-2}-1}{2}C_6(\theta) }. \]

Equivalently,

\[ \boxed{ \begin{aligned} D_m^{(6)}(\theta) ={}&-(12336\cdot3^{m-2}+2256)s^2\\ &+(1440\cdot3^{m-2}-96)cs^2 -384s^3. \end{aligned} } \]

At \(\theta=\pi\), the recurrence coefficient is \(C_6(\pi)=5280\).

Proof boundary. The recurrence for \(m\ge3\) is proved in Lean. The exceptional \(m=2\to3\) transition is certified by exact Gaussian-integer polynomial arithmetic in computational/p6_level3_orientation_certificate.py and tested in tests/test_higher_moments.py. This finite bridge is exact symbolic evidence, but it is not yet a Lean-kernel theorem.

On \(SG(1)\), the exact length-six walk classification gives 66 walks in each one-triangle class, 168 in each two-triangle class, and 486 walks visiting all three elementary triangles. The first two groups contribute zero; the all-three-triangle group contributes nonzero. This is a finite-level path-class result, not an all-level path-class theorem.

docs.title: 6.2 Eighth moment
docs.text:
For \(D_m^{(8)}(\theta)\), Lean proves

\[ D_{m+1}^{(8)}(\theta) =3D_m^{(8)}(\theta)+C_8(\theta), \qquad m\ge3. \]

The exact certificate gives

\[ \begin{aligned} D_2^{(8)}(\theta) ={}&-1335552s^2+244352cs^2-40064s^3\\ &+64cs^3+1920s^4, \end{aligned} \]

and

\[ \begin{aligned} C_8(\theta) ={}&193600s^2+75776cs^2+83712s^3\\ &-512cs^3+192s^4. \end{aligned} \]

For every \(m\ge2\),

\[ \boxed{ D_m^{(8)}(\theta) =3^{m-2}D_2^{(8)}(\theta) +\frac{3^{m-2}-1}{2}C_8(\theta) }. \]

At \(\theta=\pi\), \(C_8(\pi)=277504\).

Proof boundary. The recurrence is Lean-formalized for \(m\ge3\). The exceptional \(m=2\to3\) identity is computed coefficient-by-coefficient over Gaussian integers in computational/p8_base_certificate.py. It is exact and reproducible, but not yet a Lean-kernel theorem.

docs.title: 6.3 Tenth moment
docs.text:
The tenth-moment development contains an ordered \(p=10\) trace expansion, exact word-stratum reductions, gluing assembly, orientation recurrences, and transport of the required corner rows through degree nine.

The proposition H10TransportAll is proved by H10TransportAll_proved for both the face-axis and fixed-\(z\) configurations at every \(m\ge4\). Lean therefore proves unconditionally

\[ \boxed{ D_{m+1}^{(10)}(\theta) =3D_m^{(10)}(\theta)+C_{10}^{(5)}(\theta), \qquad m\ge4 }. \]

The corresponding affine form is

\[ \boxed{ D_m^{(10)}(\theta) =3^{m-5}\left( D_5^{(10)}(\theta)+\frac{C_{10}^{(5)}(\theta)}{2} \right) -\frac{C_{10}^{(5)}(\theta)}{2}, \qquad m\ge5 }. \]

The exact correction \(C_{10}^{(5)}(\theta)\) is the finite trace expression named defectO10_num_residual_constant. It has not yet been expanded as a trigonometric polynomial. This is a presentation task, not a remaining hypothesis in the recurrence theorem.

docs.title: 7. Numerical and exact-computation records
docs.text:
At \(\theta=\pi/2\), direct fourth-moment matrix calculations give:

\(m\) \(\dim\mathcal H_m\) \(I_m(\pi/2)\) 1 12 \(-1.333333\) 2 30 \(-1.066667\) 3 84 \(-0.952381\) 4 246 \(-0.910569\) 5 732 \(-0.896175\) 6 2190 \(-0.891324\) 7 6564 \(-0.889701\)

The Python tests also check selected vertex-wise gauge transformations. At level three, the recorded maximum spectral discrepancy is \(7.99\times10^{-15}\); the fourth-moment difference is zero at displayed precision. These checks are not assumptions in the Lean theorem.

docs.title: 9. Limitations and non-claims
docs.text:
1. No full-spectrum formula. The fourth-moment trace identity does not determine all eigenvalues or the complete spectral distribution.
  2. No spectral-gap theorem. No conclusion about the smallest positive eigenvalue follows from this identity alone.
  3. No complexity-theory result. The closed form evaluates the scalar trace defect without constructing the full matrix. This is not a complexity-class separation, lower bound, or bit-complexity theorem.
  4. No silent change of orientation. A different edge orientation defines a different operator family.
  5. No automatic extension to higher moments. Each higher moment requires its own recurrence and boundary argument.
  6. No conflation of evidence. Lean theorems, exact external certificates, and floating-point regressions are distinct.
  7. No cross-project identification. This work does not identify the SU(2) operators with signed \(Z_2\)-flux or spectral-decimation models.
  8. No physical-law claim. All statements concern the graph operators defined in the primary project.

The six-criterion protocol in the primary repository is a project-defined diagnostic for the normalized H⁴ invariant. It is not an external peer-review verdict and does not replace the theorem or its proof.

docs.title: 10. Conclusion
docs.text:
For the specified Sierpiński-gasket graph and vertex-index-oriented SU(2) connection, the fourth-moment trace defect has the exact all-level, all-angle formula

\[ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right) \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The result is machine-checked in Lean 4. Its normalized form has an exact limit and a fully explicit finite-level remainder. The H⁶ and H⁸ developments combine Lean recurrences with exact finite transition certificates; the H¹⁰ recurrence and affine form are unconditional Lean theorems.

This document consolidates the proved fourth-moment theorem and the current higher-moment advances. It does not claim that every related spectral question is closed. The full spectrum, spectral gap, Lean formalization of the H⁶/H⁸ finite bridges, and explicit trigonometric simplification of the H¹⁰ correction remain outside the principal H⁴ theorem.

docs.title: 1. Where these programmes sit
docs.text:
UltraCore-RFT is the documentation and coordination hub. The programmes below are distinct application research tracks with their own repositories, assumptions, code, tests, and licensing terms. They are not corollaries of the fourth-moment theorem, and no mathematical or engineering result should be transferred between them without an explicit derivation and evidence.

Track Primary source Current description What is not established by the repository description Quantum-processing architecture RFT-QPU-Sierpinski A proposed graph-based architecture using self-similar Sierpiński-gasket connectivity, SU(2)-valued edge transport, and a candidate two-dimensional logical subspace. The repository includes a minimal research simulator and a patent-oriented technical disclosure for counsel review. A fabricated or experimentally validated device; fault tolerance; measured gate fidelity; universal noise protection; demonstrated quantum advantage or speed-up; patent grant or established patentability. docs.title: 2. RFT-QPU-Sierpinski
docs.text:
The source repository proposes connecting self-similar graph geometry with non-Abelian SU(2) transport and projected logical controls. Its documentation describes a pre-experimental architecture, not a completed quantum processor.

The repository reports a minimal numerical core and lists a validation programme that includes logical-subspace isolation, leakage separation, projected-control independence, calibration sensitivity, disorder, thermal effects, readout, crosstalk, and scaling. These are validation obligations, not results that should be presumed complete.

  • Primary source: repository README
  • Technical disclosure: PATENT_SPEC.md
  • Source-repository terms: LICENSE.md

The patent-oriented document is a technical disclosure for qualified counsel to review. It is not a legal opinion, a patent application receipt, a granted patent, or a conclusion that any claim meets novelty, inventive-step/non-obviousness, enablement, ownership, or other legal requirements.

docs.title: 3. RFT-Invariant-Battery
docs.text:
The source repository studies an invariant-gated state-transition pattern:

measure → state → invariant gate → allowed transition → execute → verify

It reports a 10,000-km vehicle/energy-system scenario under a deliberately high 1,500 Wh/kg pack-level energy-density research sweep. The README reports 2.761 MWh for a baseline scenario, 3.205 MWh for an adverse scenario, and 2.716 MWh for a bounded-controller hypothesis. These are model outputs under stated assumptions, not measured pack performance or experimental proof of the controller's benefit.

  • Primary source: RFT-Invariant-Battery. repository
  • Source-repository terms: LICENSE.md

The project itself states that it has not established a physical 10,000-km battery, new cell chemistry, validated BMS controller, safety certification, or experimental benefit from invariant-driven control. This status must remain explicit in public descriptions.

docs.title: 4. RFT-Cosmology-Genesis
docs.text:
The source repository records a reproducible Pass-1 phenomenological calculation using the stated invariant

\[ I_m(\theta)=-16\frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad q_m=1+\epsilon I_m(\theta). \]

The repository now has a proposed analytic statement for the exact limit and finite-level remainder:

\[ I_\infty(\theta)=-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The theorem document and regression tests are being reviewed in the source repository's PR #1. The source PR's CI has passed, but human review and merge remain pending. This hub treats the statement as an analytic result under review, not as a merged release or Lean-formalized theorem.

The cosmology repository itself explicitly limits its scope: the coupling is phenomenological; the acoustic calculation is reduced; baseline acoustic multipoles are reference values; and no full CMB likelihood is implemented. No observational detection, new physical law, or physical origin for \(\epsilon\) is claimed.

  • Primary source: RFT-Cosmology-Genesis
  • Model specification: MODEL_SPEC.md
  • Limitations: LIMITATIONS.md
  • Theorem review: PR #1

docs.title: 5. Evidence and claim boundaries
docs.text:
Use these labels consistently across the programme:

  • Formal theorem: a proposition proved in a specified formal system for its exact definitions and assumptions.
  • Numerically reproduced: a computational result tied to named code, inputs, parameters, tolerances, and outputs.
  • Engineering-tested: a claim supported by tests or experiments for a specified implementation and configuration.
  • Research architecture: a proposed design whose key physical or operational requirements remain to be validated.
  • Modelled scenario: an output of a model under declared assumptions; not a physical measurement.
  • Patent-oriented disclosure: technical material organized for counsel review; not a statement of patent grant, patentability, priority, or freedom to operate.

A successful test suite, an attractive banner, a numerical fit, or a patent-oriented document cannot by itself promote a claim to a stronger evidence category. Report unresolved validation items rather than silently treating them as complete.

docs.title: 6. Attribution, licensing, and public-disclosure discipline
docs.text:
The QPU and Invariant Battery source repositories publish their own LICENSE.md files describing Business 1.0 proprietary / all-rights-reserved terms. Cosmology-Genesis declares Apache-2.0. All upstream licenses remain separate from the Apache-2.0 license for original UltraCore-RFT content.

Accordingly, this hub provides source links and short factual descriptions; it does not copy source code, figures, tables, or substantial passages from those repositories. The UltraCore-RFT license must not be read as relicensing upstream project materials. Permission to reuse third-party material must be checked against the relevant source license and, where necessary, obtained in writing from the rights holder.

Public GitHub publication is not a substitute for an IP strategy. Before making further disclosures or relying on a patent position, obtain qualified advice on ownership and inventorship, prior art, filing dates and jurisdictions, claim scope, enablement, licensing, confidentiality, and any applicable disclosure deadlines. This page is a documentation record, not legal advice and not a determination that any invention is patentable or protected.

No employment, partnership, institutional sponsorship, endorsement, regulatory approval, or commercial readiness is implied by inclusion in this index.

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text: RFT-SIRM separates research claims, mathematical definitions, executable implementations, and verification evidence. Engineering components should enforce their specified invariants and reject invalid state transitions atomically where the implementation supports that guarantee. Guarantees are scoped to the relevant code, threat model, and tests; documentation must not imply that every component or research result is formally verified.

docs.title: 1. Evgeny's Theorem: a formalized fourth-moment result
docs.text:
Primary sources: source repository, theorem statement, Lean formalization, and verification record.

For the specific operator definitions and assumptions in that project, the stated identity is

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\geq1. \]

The source project reports a Lean 4 formalization. The scope of that formalization is the encoded proposition and its definitions. It does not, by itself, prove the higher-moment recurrence, the signed-flux decimation criterion, SIRM runtime invariants, or a physical interpretation.

docs.title: 2. Evgeny's Theory of Everything: higher-moment recurrence programme
docs.text:
Primary sources: repository, dissertation, final status, and claims and evidence.

This programme studies trace defects for higher even moments \(H^6\), \(H^8\), and \(H^{10}\), including Fourier-coefficient candidates, exact finite-level modular/CRT certificates, and independent sparse-matrix numerical holdouts. The repository reports checks through level 7 for specified finite sets of angles and a pinned Lean build for the upstream fourth-moment result. These are distinct evidence types. The universal all-level higher-moment recurrence remains open: finite certificates and numerical agreement do not establish it.

docs.title: 3. Phi-Genesis: signed-flux spectral analysis
docs.text:
Primary sources: repository, verified results, research map, and reproducibility guide.

Phi-Genesis investigates signed \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-flux graph Laplacians on Sierpiński-gasket approximations, spectral decimation, spectral gaps, boundary/corner corrections, inertia-based counting, and exploratory integer mass-index patterns. The factor-5 decimation structure is reported with boundary/corner qualifications. Gate A remains open because the full exceptional set and all residual mismatches have not been explained. The proposed index set \(\{1,12,17,40\}\) is not established as a predictive selection law. The signed-flux operators are not assumed equivalent to the SU(2)-connected operators in Evgeny's Theorem.

docs.title: 4. RFT-QPU-Sierpinski: proposed quantum-processing architecture
docs.text:
Primary source: RFT-QPU-Sierpinski, including its repository status, validation plan, and evidence boundary.

The proposed level-1 Sierpiński tile has 6 graph sites, 9 graph edges, 3 selected non-commuting X/Y/Z SU(2) links, 12 transmon modes, and 22 effective exchange channels. A candidate logical qubit is encoded in a selected two-dimensional low-energy subspace. Stage 11B contains a re-quantized three-mode A–coupler–B gate-model study and local pulse retuning.

The reported five-level/480-grid local process overlap and average logical-state fidelity are closed-system projections of that three-mode model. They are not measured gate fidelities and do not constitute a full driven simulation of the 12-mode tile. No chip has been fabricated or measured. The complex-Z edge, multi-tone plan, open-system noise, device-specific circuit extraction, and one-/two-cell hardware demonstrations remain open. The source repository is licensed separately under BUSL-1.1; this hub's Apache-2.0 licence does not relicense it.

docs.title: 5. SIRM Financial Infrastructure: formal financial-state model
docs.text:
Primary source: SIRM-Financial-Infrastructure · formalization status · mathematical scope.

This dedicated Lean 4.33.1 workstream formalizes financial state and admissible transitions. Its combined authorized financial machine updates holder balances and the corresponding signed general-ledger journal together in one abstract state transition. Additional modules cover authority and account-control gates, typed account/asset registries, exact base-unit and migration arithmetic with residual carry-forward, per-principal nonces and typed request receipts, cached denial responses, concurrent pooled escrow, discrete time-lock expiry, and first-stage per-ID dispute freeze.

The repository's CI is configured as one Lean build/theorem-test job plus 17 static audits. This describes the workflow structure; individual results must be cited against their exact commit and run. The model does not yet prove production database persistence/atomicity, cryptographic signatures, key custody, reserve backing, external settlement, legal ownership, regulatory compliance, or Lean-to-Rust refinement. The Rust reference implementation is planned, not complete. The older runtime-invariant strand described below is a separate systems model and should not be conflated with this financial specification.

docs.title: 6. RFT-Cosmology-Genesis: exact invariant and phenomenological extension
docs.text:
Primary sources: repository, exact invariant remainder theorem, model specification, results, and limitations.

For the normalized invariant defined in that repository,

\[ I_m(\theta)=-16\frac{3^{m-1}+1}{3^{m+1}+3}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \]

the exact limit and finite-level remainder are

\[ I_\infty(\theta)=-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The repository records an algebraic derivation and Lean-checked results for the stated invariant. Its photon-sector coupling and background/CMB response are phenomenological. No physical origin for the coupling, detection of a new interaction, or agreement with a full observational CMB likelihood is established by this mathematical identity.

docs.title: 7. SIRM runtime-invariant engineering architecture
docs.text: SIRM is the Synthetic Intelligence Reasoning Model. In the engineering repositories, the operational core is a state-transition model constrained by explicit invariants, arithmetic checks, permission boundaries, and reproducible tests. These implementation-level constraints must be documented and verified against the actual code. They are not consequences of the spectral trace identity unless a separate formal connection is stated and proved.

docs.text:

Each source repository remains authoritative for the exact statement, formal proof, finite certificate, numerical experiment, validation gate, and remaining limitations.

docs.title: 4.1 Methodology
docs.text:
We constructed a discrete-event simulation that models GreedyScheduler behavior under controlled contention patterns. The simulation is not a production validator measurement — it is a reference model designed to isolate and observe scheduling behavior under specific workload assumptions.

Simulation parameters: - Priority queue (max-heap by compute_unit_price) - Thread-aware account locks (write/read conflict detection) - Per-pass execution model: scheduled transactions hold locks for one pass, then release - Incoming traffic: 50 tx per scheduling pass - Worker threads: 4 - Drain passes: 200+ after input stops

docs.title: 4.2 Scenarios
docs.text: Scenario Description Conflict Intensity Sustained Contention 30% of transactions write to 5 hot accounts Moderate Burst → Independent 10 passes of burst contention, then independent transactions High → None Hot Account Priority Starvation 70% of transactions write to 1 hot account, random priorities Extreme Independent All transactions write to unique accounts None (baseline)

docs.title: Scenario: Hot Account Priority Starvation
docs.text:
Metric GreedyScheduler (reference model) Total transactions 2,000 Scheduled 835 (41.8%) Deferred (still in queue after 200+ drain passes) 1,165 (58.3%) Explicitly dropped 0 (0%) — no mechanism exists Mean scheduling latency 28.9 passes P99 scheduling latency 210 passes Max queue depth observed 1,382

Interpretation: In this synthetic model, lower-priority transactions to the hot account are deferred indefinitely while higher-priority traffic continues to be scheduled. There is no metric that would allow an operator to observe this accumulation. The transactions are not lost — they remain in the queue — but their scheduling latency is unbounded.

docs.title: Scenario: Burst → Independent
docs.text:
Metric GreedyScheduler (reference model) Scheduled 2,000 (100%) — with high latency tail Mean latency 11.4 passes P99 latency 92 passes Queue drain time after burst ends ~100 passes

Interpretation: After a burst of contention ends, the scheduler must sequentially drain a large deferred backlog before new independent transactions experience low latency.

docs.title: Scenario: Independent (baseline)
docs.text:
Metric GreedyScheduler (reference model) Scheduled 2,000 (100%) Mean latency ~0 passes P99 latency 1 pass

Interpretation: With zero conflicts, the scheduler performs optimally. No regression observed.

docs.title: 4.4 Rift Scheduler Reference Model Comparison
docs.text:
Under identical synthetic workloads, the Rift Scheduler (bounded retry semantics) demonstrates:

Metric GreedyScheduler Rift Scheduler (research) Deferred queue drain Unbounded Bounded by max_retry_count Starvation observability None dropped_transactions metric Recovery after burst ~100 passes ~40 passes Mean latency (hot priority) 28.9 passes 1.0 pass

Important: These are reference model results comparing two scheduling semantics under identical synthetic assumptions. They do not constitute a claim that Rift Scheduler is superior in all production scenarios.

docs.title: 5. Coverage Stabilization
docs.text: Coverage typically stabilizes within the first 100,000 executions (cov: ~420 ft: ~2600 for the scheduler). Subsequent runs refine the corpus but rarely discover new coverage, indicating the harness has exhausted the reachable state space for inputs within the size limits.

docs.title: 6.1 Fuzzing
docs.text: Fuzzing explores the input space stochastically. A 5h 55m run increases confidence that no invariant violation exists for inputs of the tested size and shape. It does not constitute a formal proof. Formal verification (model checking or theorem proving) is planned for Phase 4.

docs.title: 6.2 Synthetic Benchmark
docs.text: The scheduler benchmark is a discrete-event simulation, not a measurement from a production validator or mainnet traffic. Results are valid under the stated assumptions (50 tx/pass, 4 threads, random priorities, specific contention ratios). Real-world validator behavior may differ due to: - Network latency and jitter - Variable transaction arrival patterns - CU budget constraints not modeled in the simulation - Hardware differences (NUMA, cache hierarchy)

docs.title: 6.3 General
docs.text: No verification method can exhaustively prove absence of bugs. Our approach is defense in depth: unit tests catch obvious errors, fuzzing catches edge cases, synthetic benchmarks model specific scenarios, and formal verification (planned) will provide machine-checked proofs for critical invariants.

docs.title: Field Trial: seL4 Capability Derivation Tree Stress-Verification
docs.text: Document ID: RFT-EXP-SELC4-2026-001 Date: 2026-08-03 Laboratory: RFT-SIRM / UltraCore-RFT Classification: Reproducible Research Artifact Revision: Final

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
This report documents a deterministic empirical verification experiment in which the UltraCore-RFT stress-testing methodology was applied to the Capability Derivation Tree (CDT) of the seL4 microkernel. The experiment executed more than one billion pseudo-random, syntactically valid capability operations under deterministic seed control. No kernel crashes, panics, or allocator-level invariant violations were observed during the monitored execution. The seL4 test suite completed successfully after the marathon phase.

Disclaimer: This experiment does not claim to prove, improve, or replace the formal verification of seL4. It records only observable, reproducible behavior under sustained load.

docs.title: 1. Objective
docs.text:
To empirically observe the stability and resource reclamation behavior of the seL4 CDT implementation when subjected to a sustained sequence of valid capability invocations generated by a deterministic, seed-controlled pseudo-random process.

Working Hypothesis:

Under a deterministic pseudo-random sequence of syntactically valid capability invocations, the seL4 CDT implementation does not produce kernel panics, unrecoverable page faults, or VKA-level memory leaks detectable by the test harness.

This hypothesis is empirically falsifiable and does not constitute a mathematical theorem about seL4 correctness.

docs.title: 6. Relationship to UltraCore-RFT
docs.text:
This experiment demonstrates that the deterministic empirical verification methodology developed within UltraCore-RFT / SIRM is transferable from the blockchain runtime layer to the operating-system layer.

The SIRM core methodology:

  1. Deterministic seed control — every state transition sequence is reproducible
  2. Invariant telemetry — quantitative metrics recorded after every batch
  3. Resource drain verification — system must return to a known clean state
  4. Complementary checking — empirical stress runs operate alongside formal specifications

The object of study is not seL4 itself, but the applicability of the methodology.

docs.title: 7. Research Contribution
docs.text: # Contribution Description 1 Deterministic empirical stress verification Seed-controlled, reproducible protocol for sustained pseudo-random valid load 2 Repeatable capability verification methodology Documented procedure: build → run → drain → measure 3 Complementary verification alongside formal proofs Empirical layer checking runtime invariants without asserting specification coverage 4 CI-ready kernel regression methodology Lightweight harness integrable into CI pipelines 5 Reusable research framework Single-file drop-in module for sel4test, adaptable to custom extensions

docs.title: 8. Limitations
docs.text:
1. Empirical, not mathematical. This experiment provides observational data. It does not constitute a formal proof of seL4 correctness, nor does it replace the existing Isabelle/HOL proof.
  2. Valid-input only. Only syntactically correct, ABI-compliant invocations were used. Malformed system calls, invalid capability encodings, and kernel binary fuzzing were excluded.
  3. Limited object coverage. Only Endpoint, Notification, and TCB objects were retyped. Page tables, ASID pools, frames, IRQ control, and device untypeds were not tested.
  4. Single-threaded. No concurrency, inter-CPU races, or multi-process capability transfers were exercised.
  5. Emulated hardware. QEMU virt was used. Timing, cache behavior, and memory-ordering effects on physical silicon may differ.
  6. Observational ceiling. A zero-fault result over 10⁹ operations does not imply that the 10⁹+1-th operation cannot fail. It is a statistical sample, not an exhaustive enumeration.

docs.title: Core Invariants
docs.text: The SIRM (Stable Invariant Resource Model) defines four hard constraints that every RFT-SIRM system must satisfy after every state-mutating operation.

docs.title: I1: Supply Conservation
docs.text:
total_supply = total_base_sum + global_field * p

Where: - total_supply — total economic supply in the system - total_base_sum — sum of all individual base balances - global_field — uniform scalar shift applied to all participants - p — number of active participants

The total supply is decomposed into a uniform field component (global_field * p) and individual deviations (total_base_sum). This decomposition enables O(1) redistribution.

docs.title: I2: Mint/Burn Accounting
docs.text:
total_supply = total_minted - total_burned

Supply is strictly derived from minted and burned amounts. No implicit inflation or deflation paths exist.

docs.title: I3: Dust Bound
docs.text:
dust_accumulator < p (when p > 0)

Dust (rounding remainder from division operations) is bounded by participant count. When p decreases (unregister), dust is re-normalized to maintain the bound.

docs.title: I4: Debt Limit
docs.text:
effective_balance[i] >= -(total_supply / 10p)

Where effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field.

No participant can accumulate debt beyond a fraction of total supply. The factor of 10 is a protocol parameter.

docs.title: Standard Model
docs.text:
In typical distributed systems, distributing a reward R to p participants requires:

for i in 0..p:
    balance[i] += R / p    -- O(p) operations

At p = 1,000,000, this is 1,000,000 storage writes.

docs.title: RFT Model
docs.text:
In RFT-SIRM, distribution is a single scalar update:

global_field += R / p    -- O(1) operation

All participants' effective balances increase by R / p simultaneously because effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field.

This is a different mathematical model, not an optimization.

docs.title: Effective Balance
docs.text:
effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field
  • base_balance[i] — individual deviation from the uniform field
  • global_field — shared scalar shift

docs.title: Transfer with Edge Cost
docs.text:
// From sender
delta_from = amount + edge_cost
base_balance[from] -= delta_from

// To receiver
delta_to = amount
base_balance[to] += delta_to

// Edge cost handling
if edge_cost > 0:
    // Burn: reduce total supply
    total_supply -= edge_cost
elif edge_cost < 0:
    // Mint: increase total supply
    total_supply += |edge_cost|

Edge cost is a protocol-level mechanism for directed taxation or subsidization.

docs.title: Negative Entropy
docs.text:
// Deflationary tick
global_field -= e * 10^18  // where e is Euler's number

// Compensate total_base_sum to preserve I1
total_base_sum += e * 10^18 * p

This creates deflationary pressure on effective balances while preserving the supply invariant.

docs.title: Evgeny's Theorem: An Exact Spectral Identity
docs.text: Unlike the operational analogies above, this section states a concrete mathematical result about a concrete object. It is independent of the runtime modeling language used elsewhere in this document. Source, tests and data: RFT-SIRM/Evgeny-Theorem.

docs.title: Object
docs.text:
SG(m) is the Sierpiński-gasket graph at refinement level m, with n(m) = (3^(m+1) + 3) / 2 vertices and 3^m elementary triangles. The Hilbert space is C^n ⊗ C². Every edge carries an SU(2) unitary, and flux is injected through one designated edge per triangle. Two configurations are compared at the same angle θ:

  • C (non-commuting): the rotation axis cycles x / y / z by triangle index, so holonomies of neighbouring triangles genuinely do not commute.
  • C′ (commuting control): the axis is fixed to z, which is exactly two decoupled U(1) copies.

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
Δ_m(H⁴, θ) = Tr(H_C⁴) − Tr(H_C′⁴) = −16 · (3^(m−1) + 1) · sin²(θ/2)

Normalizing by dim(H) = 3^(m+1) + 3 gives the intensive invariant I_m(θ), which converges to −(16/9) · sin²(θ/2). At θ = π/2 the limit is exactly −8/9.

m dim(H) Δ_m(H⁴, π/2) I_m(π/2) 1 12 −16 −1.333333 3 84 −80 −0.952381 5 732 −656 −0.896175 7 6,564 −5,840 −0.889701

The defect vanishes exactly for the moments p = 1, 2, 3 and first appears at p = 4, so a single gauge-invariant spectral moment separates a non-Abelian connection from its commuting control.

docs.title: Verification Status
docs.text: Statement Status The closed form matches direct computation for every tested (m, θ), m = 1…7 (held-out pairs, θ-grid, level 7) Established (reproducible) The fourth moment is gauge-invariant under random SU(2) gauge transformations Established (spectrum change ≤ 8 × 10⁻¹⁵) The closed form holds for all m ≥ 1 and θ Machine-checked in Lean 4 (concrete operators, fourth moment; no sorry, standard axioms only) Lean 4 formalization Complete for the stated scope (formalization/README.md); independent review of the formal definitions pending

docs.title: Scope and Limits
docs.text:
• The closed form applies strictly to the fourth moment. It is not a statement about the full spectrum, the spectral gap, or any other moment.
  • It is not a physical theory, and it does not address the Yang–Mills existence-and-mass-gap problem or any other Millennium Prize Problem.
  • Relationship to SIRM: the two share a methodology (state the invariant first, then test it at every scale, with held-out checks). There is currently no mathematical derivation connecting the theorem to the runtime invariants I1–I4.

docs.title: 3. SIRM Core: The Mathematical Foundation
docs.text:
All RFT-SIRM systems are instances of a single deterministic state machine:

State  = (total_supply, total_base_sum, global_field, p, dust_accumulator, base_balance[])

I1: total_supply = total_base_sum + global_field * p
I2: total_supply = total_minted - total_burned
I3: dust_accumulator < p  (when p > 0)
I4: effective_balance[i] >= -(total_supply / 10p)

where effective_balance[i] = base_balance[i] + global_field

Key property: global_field is a scalar. Updating it by Δ changes every participant's effective balance by Δ simultaneously — O(1) regardless of participant count. No iteration. No per-account writes. Deterministic and verifiable.

docs.title: 3.3 Agave Memory Contexts
docs.text:
Property Value Role SVM memory isolation and CPI security research Language Rust Status Active research — bug reported upstream Repository RFT-SIRM/agave-abiv2-memory-contexts Upstream anza-xyz/svm#25 Key Finding CPI permission leakage: per-frame writable permission rollback failure

Problem: During CPI execution in Agave SVM, multiple update_account_permissions calls within a single frame destroyed rollback entries from earlier calls. On pop(), only the last-touched account was restored; earlier accounts retained modified permissions permanently.

Impact: Writable permissions could leak across CPI boundaries, violating isolation guarantees.

Fix: Record each account's pre-frame value only on its first touch within the frame, never overwriting on subsequent calls.

docs.title: 3.4 Agave Scheduler
docs.text:
Property Value Role Conflict-aware transaction scheduling research Language Rust Status RFC published — upstream discussion open Repository RFT-SIRM/agave-rift-scheduler Upstream anza-xyz/agave#14274 Key Finding GreedyScheduler deferred queue lacks retry bound and starvation observability

Observation: GreedyScheduler in Agave defers conflicting transactions by re-inserting them into the priority queue without a per-transaction retry counter, a configurable upper bound, or a dropped_transactions metric.

Impact: Under sustained write contention on a hot account, lower-priority transactions may be deferred indefinitely. They are not lost from the queue, but their scheduling latency is unbounded and unobservable.

Proposal: Add max_retry_count (configurable) and dropped_transactions metric to GreedySchedulerConfig / SchedulingSummary. ~15 lines. No policy change.

Verification: Rift Scheduler reference implementation enforces bounded retry semantics with I1–I4 invariants. 91M+ fuzz executions, 0 violations.

docs.title: 1. Focused mathematical dissertation
docs.text:
Spectral Trace Defects of Noncommutative SU(2) Connections on Sierpiński-Gasket Graphs

Primary project: RFT-SIRM/Evgeny-Theorem Date: 9 November 2026 (UltraCore edition) Scope: the specified non-commuting SU(2)-connected operator on Sierpiński-gasket graphs and its commuting control.

The central result is the exact fourth-moment trace-defect identity

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\ge1,\ \theta\in\mathbb R. \]

After normalization by the Hilbert-space dimension \(3^{m+1}+3\),

\[ I_\infty(\theta) =\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3} =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

The focused UltraCore dissertation is a theorem-centred edition prepared from the primary source records. The machine-checked Lean declarations, computational scripts, and detailed source history remain in Evgeny-Theorem. It also documents the distinct proof status of H⁶, H⁸, and H¹⁰. The H⁴ statement is the primary all-level theorem; higher moments must be cited at their own levels and with their own proof boundaries.

Primary verification sources: THEOREM.md · Lean formalization · VERIFICATION.md · higher-moment status.

The programme then branches into invariant-based systems engineering and applications. UltraCore's engineering identity remains a deterministic execution architecture—not because the blockchain is the foundation, but because the runtime work is one downstream implementation strand. docs.title: 1. The Transition
docs.text:
The ecosystem contains two connected but distinct kinds of work: literal mathematical research and systems engineering. The mathematical strand includes a specific fourth-moment identity reported as machine-checked in Lean 4, higher-moment extensions that remain open at the all-level stage, and a separate signed-flux spectral-decimation audit. The systems strand applies invariant-first design to deterministic state transitions, runtimes, protocols, and verification.

The correct hierarchy is therefore not “blockchain first.” It is definitions and theorem → evidence and open questions → engineering methodology → implementations and exploratory applications. The arrows express a reading order and research motivation, not a claim that the theorem proves the applications.

This document explains the execution-platform strand within that larger research programme.

docs.title: 2. What UltraCore Is Not
docs.text: Understanding the platform requires first clearing away mischaracterizations.

docs.title: Not an Operating System
docs.text: An operating system manages hardware resources, process scheduling, device drivers, and user-space interfaces. UltraCore operates at a different layer: it is an execution substrate that coordinates deterministic state transitions across distributed nodes. It can theoretically operate above different verified system kernels — Linux, seL4, or future deterministic kernels — but it does not replace them.

docs.title: Not "Another Blockchain"
docs.text: While the Rift-L1 Blockchain and Rift Network are concrete implementations, the blockchain is one application of the execution architecture, not its defining identity. The same deterministic invariant model can govern validator infrastructure, execution runtimes, distributed systems, and high-assurance computing environments without ever issuing a token or producing a block.

docs.title: Not a Completed Physical Theory of Everything
docs.text: The title of the Evgeny's Theory of Everything repository names a broad research programme; it does not claim that a complete physical theory of the Universe has been proved. The fourth-moment theorem in Evgeny-Theorem is a literal mathematical statement about defined operators and is reported as formalized in Lean 4. The all-level higher-moment recurrence remains open, and Phi-Genesis studies a separate signed-flux operator family. Physical vocabulary used elsewhere in RFT documents remains modelling language unless supported by a separate physical theory and evidence. See Scientific Basis and the AI Guide.

docs.title: 5. Why seL4 Research Matters
docs.text:
The seL4 Capability Derivation Tree (CDT) verification work is frequently misread. This section clarifies its actual role.

What it was: Complementary engineering research. The laboratory explored formally verified kernels to understand deterministic execution environments at the operating-system layer. The goal was methodological — understanding how deterministic invariant systems behave when applied to a formally verified substrate — not architectural.

What it was not: A claim that UltraCore currently runs on seL4, or that seL4 is a dependency of any UltraCore implementation. No production deployment on seL4 exists. No roadmap milestone requires seL4.

What it enables: Three things:

  1. Methodological transferability. The SIRM deterministic verification protocol (seed-controlled fuzzing, invariant telemetry, resource drain verification) was successfully transferred from blockchain runtimes to OS kernels. This demonstrates that the methodology is domain-independent.
  2. Future deployment path. Should a future version of UltraCore Runtime require a formally verified kernel substrate, seL4 represents a known, tested integration point — not a requirement, but an option.
  3. Research credibility. Independent validation of a formally verified system through empirical stress-testing strengthens the laboratory's verification culture. It shows that the team understands both formal methods and empirical methods, and does not conflate them.

See SEL4_CDT_FUZZING.md and seL4 CDT Verification for the full experimental report, including limitations.

docs.text:
The engineering vision is to explore deterministic, invariant-governed execution in several environments:

docs.title: 2. Mathematical anchor: the fourth-moment identity
docs.text:
For the definitions and assumptions documented by the primary theorem repository,

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m=1,2,3,\ldots. \]

With the source's normalization, the exact finite-level formula is

\[ I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) -\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

Thus

\[ I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_\infty\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\frac89. \]

docs.title: Algebraic sanity checks
docs.text:
• \(3^{m+1}+3=3(3^m+1)\).
  • At \(m=1,\theta=\pi/2\): \(\Delta_1=-16\), dimension \(=12\), and \(I_1=-4/3\).
  • The exact finite-level remainder is \(-32\sin^2(\theta/2)/(9(3^m+1))\).

The source repository reports that the fourth-moment statement is formalized in Lean 4 for the concrete operators and the quantifiers in the formal theorem. A checked formal proposition does not by itself settle independent semantic review, peer review, or novelty relative to the literature.

Primary sources: focused theorem dissertation · theorem statement · Lean formalization · verification record.

docs.title: 3. Higher moments: report each theorem at its own scope
docs.text:
The current primary-source status differs by moment:

  • H⁶ and H⁸: Lean proves the all-angle recurrences for \(m\ge3\). Exact symbolic certificates supply the exceptional \(m=2\to3\) transitions and combined formulas for \(m\ge2\), but the finite bridges are not yet Lean-kernel theorems.
  • H¹⁰: Lean proves the radius-four transport and the unconditional affine recurrence for \(m\ge4\), with the affine formula for \(m\ge5\). The level-five correction remains an exact finite trace expression.
  • General extension: a unified all-level recurrence theorem covering the broader higher-moment family remains open.

A finite certificate proves its stated finite claim, not an infinite family. Numerical holdouts and sparse-matrix-power checks remain finite computational evidence. Do not use the H⁴ proof as if it proved H⁶/H⁸/H¹⁰, and do not flatten the distinct higher-moment proof statuses into one label.

docs.title: 4. Phi-Genesis: a separate operator family
docs.text: Phi-Genesis studies signed \(Z_2\)-flux graph Laplacians, Schur elimination, spectral decimation, boundary/corner corrections, inertia, and exploratory mass-index patterns. This is not the SU(2) operator family in Evgeny's Theorem.

docs.title: Proved spectral result
docs.text:
For the signless Laplacian \(Q_N\) of the level-\(N\) Sierpiński-gasket graph and its diagonal-gauge-conjugate signed matrix, the Lean development proves for every \(N=6+n\):

  • the canonical A1 root is an eigenvalue and no eigenvalue is smaller;
  • the least eigenvalue is the unique A1 root in the fixed bootstrap interval;
  • the sequence of least eigenvalues converges to a limit in the exact rational interval
\[ \left[ \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}}, \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}} \right]. \]

The interval width is \(2\times10^{-36}\). In decimal notation, the certified enclosure is

\[ 1.309128920280813421888623088170810187 \le\lambda_\infty\le 1.309128920280813421888623088170810189. \]

The midpoint is approximately \(1.309128920280813421888623088170810188\). This is the limiting least-eigenvalue value for the specified graph-matrix sequence, not a known fundamental physical constant.

The result is recorded in SchurEigenvalue.lean and transferred to the signed matrix in SchurSignedTransfer.lean. See also PR #31 and PR #32.

docs.title: 7. SIRM runtime model and invariants
docs.text:
SIRM specifies runtime constraints for deterministic state transitions. The compact notation below is mapped to implementation variables immediately afterward.

\[ \begin{aligned} I_1:\quad & S = B + Gp,\\ I_2:\quad & S = M - D,\\ I_3:\quad & d < p \quad (p>0),\\ I_4:\quad & E_i \ge -\frac{S}{10p}. \end{aligned} \]

The effective-balance relation is

\[ E_i = b_i + G. \] Symbol Implementation variable \(S\) total_supply \(B\) total_base_sum \(G\) global_field \(M\) total_minted \(D\) total_burned \(d\) dust_accumulator \(E_i\) effective_balance[i] \(b_i\) base_balance[i]

Where \(\mathtt{effective\_balance}[i]=\mathtt{base\_balance}[i]+\mathtt{global\_field}\), under the model's integer and scaling conventions.

The \(O(1)\) distribution argument concerns a shared scalar update and lazy effective-balance calculation. It does not imply every operation is \(O(1)\), nor does the spectral theorem prove the SIRM invariants. Runtime tests, fuzzing, audits, and deployment evidence have implementation-specific scope.

docs.title: Mathematical Results and Evidence Register
docs.text:
This page is the compact technical reference for the mathematical results presented by UltraCore-RFT. Each result is attached to its own operator family, quantifiers, proof artifacts, and limitations. The SU(2) connection operators, the signed \(Z_2\)-flux graph matrices, and the SIRM runtime model are separate mathematical or engineering objects.

H⁴ All-level SU(2) trace-defect identity, \(m\ge1\)

H⁶ / H⁸ / H¹⁰ Lean recurrences with distinct starting levels and finite-bridge boundaries

\(\lambda_\infty\) Phi-Genesis least-eigenvalue limit, levels \(N\ge6\)

docs.title: 1. SU(2) connection operators: the fourth moment
docs.text:
For the specific non-commuting SU(2) connection \(C\) and commuting control \(C'\) defined in the primary project, the fourth-moment trace defect is

\[ \boxed{ \Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta) =\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_C(m,\theta)^4\right) -\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(H_{C'}(m,\theta)^4\right) =-16\left(3^{m-1}+1\right) \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) } \]

for every integer \(m\ge1\) and every real \(\theta\). The concrete theorem is machine-checked in Lean 4 in Evgeny-Theorem, under the definitions and assumptions recorded there.

docs.title: Normalization and finite-size correction
docs.text:
The Hilbert-space dimension is \(N_m=3^{m+1}+3\). Define

\[ I_m(\theta) =\frac{\Delta_m^{(4)}(\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3}. \]

The exact finite-level expression separates into its limit and a finite-size remainder:

\[ \boxed{ I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) -\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) } \]

Consequently,

\[ I_\infty(\theta) =\lim_{m\to\infty}I_m(\theta) =-\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \]

and the exact remainder is

\[ I_m(\theta)-I_\infty(\theta) =-\frac{32}{9(3^m+1)}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right). \]

At \(\theta=\pi/2\), the limit is exactly \(-8/9\). The finite-level error decays with the explicit factor \((3^m+1)^{-1}\); no numerical fitting is needed for this identity.

Scope of the theorem

This result concerns the specified SU(2)-connected graph operators and their commuting control. It does not, by itself, prove the higher-moment recurrences, the Phi-Genesis spectral statements, a physical law, or an engineering invariant.

Primary evidence: theorem statement · Lean formalization · verification record · focused dissertation.

docs.title: 2. Higher moments: three distinct proof boundaries
docs.text:
The higher moments are not one undifferentiated theorem. Each has its own recurrence, starting level, and exceptional finite transition.

  • Sixth moment — H⁶

    Lean proves the all-angle recurrence

    \[ D_{m+1}^{(6)}(\theta)=3D_m^{(6)}(\theta)+C_6(\theta),\quad m\ge3. \]

    The \(m=2\to3\) transition is covered by an exact symbolic certificate, not yet by a Lean-kernel theorem.

  • Eighth moment — H⁸

    Lean proves

    \[ D_{m+1}^{(8)}(\theta)=3D_m^{(8)}(\theta)+C_8(\theta),\quad m\ge3. \]

    Its exceptional \(m=2\to3\) transition also has an exact finite certificate; keep that boundary explicit.

  • Tenth moment — H¹⁰

    Lean proves the radius-four transport and unconditional affine recurrence for $m\ge4:

    \[ D_{m+1}^{(10)}(\theta)=3D_m^{(10)}(\theta)+C_{10}^{(5)}(\theta). \]

    The affine closed form applies for \(m\ge5\); the level-five correction remains an exact finite trace expression.

A unified all-level recurrence covering the broader higher-moment family remains open. Finite certificates prove their stated finite claims; numerical holdouts are not substitutes for universal proofs.

Primary evidence: higher-moment status · formalization · broader synthesis dissertation.

docs.title: 3. Phi-Genesis: a separate signed \(Z_2\)-flux graph problem
docs.text: Phi-Genesis studies signed and signless graph Laplacians, Schur elimination, spectral decimation, and boundary-corner corrections. It is not the SU(2) connection-operator family above; no operator equivalence is claimed.

docs.title: Uniform signed-Laplacian lower bound
docs.text:
For every refinement level, every real eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of the explicitly defined signed Laplacian with a nonzero real eigenvector satisfies

\[ \boxed{\lambda\ge1.} \]

The matrix definition and eigenvector hypotheses are part of the statement. This is a uniform lower bound, not the least-eigenvalue limit theorem below.

docs.title: Least-eigenvalue identification and convergence
docs.text:
For the level-\(N\) signless Laplacians \(Q_N\) and their gauge-conjugate signed matrices, the canonical A1 Schur root is identified as the least eigenvalue for \(N\ge6\). Both least-eigenvalue sequences converge to \(\lambda_\infty\) in the exact interval

\[ \boxed{ \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}} \le\lambda_\infty\le \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}} } \]

The interval width is exactly \(2\cdot10^{-36}\) and its half-width is \(10^{-36}\). Its midpoint is approximately

\[ 1.309128920280813421888623088170810188. \]

This number is the limiting least eigenvalue of the specified graph-matrix sequence. It is not known in closed form and is not claimed to be a universal physical constant.

docs.title: Parameter derivatives and the open quadratic law
docs.text:
The Lean development also proves parameter differentiability of both finite-level Schur boundary coordinates throughout the closed bootstrap interval. This is an analytic ingredient for further estimates, not the quadratic increment theorem.

Still open in Phi-Genesis

The complete Gate A exceptional-set characterization, the quadratic increment law \(\delta_{m+1}\sim c\delta_m^2\) and existence of \(c\), levels \(N<6\), a closed form for \(\lambda_\infty\), and identification with an external \(\theta=2\pi\) operator remain open. The derivative recursion does not close these problems.

Primary evidence: least-eigenvalue theorem · signed transfer · uniform lower bound · Schur derivative trajectory · proof map.

docs.title: 4. SIRM: an independent runtime-invariant model
docs.text:
SIRM expresses constraints on runtime state transitions. The notation below is the compact mathematical model; implementation-specific variable mappings and integer/scaling conventions are documented in Foundations.

\[ \begin{aligned} I_1:\quad & S=B+Gp,\\ I_2:\quad & S=M-D,\\ I_3:\quad & d<p\quad(p>0),\\ I_4:\quad & E_i\ge-\frac{S}{10p}. \end{aligned} \]

The effective balance is

\[ E_i=b_i+G. \] Symbol Meaning \(S\) Total supply \(B\) Sum of base balances \(G\) Global field / shared scalar \(p\) Participant count \(M,D\) Total minted and total burned \(d\) Dust accumulator \(E_i,b_i\) Effective and base balance of participant \(i\)

These are runtime-model invariants. They are not corollaries of the SU(2) trace identity or the Phi-Genesis graph spectrum; they require implementation-specific tests, fuzzing, audit, and deployment evidence.

docs.text:

docs.title: Development Strategy
docs.text:
Scope: Strategic roadmap, research phases, and ecosystem positioning for the RFT-SIRM deterministic invariant systems laboratory.

Dated status snapshot: 9 November 2026. This file preserves earlier programme phases as an archival planning record while the current priorities track the proved H⁴, H⁶/H⁸/H¹⁰, and Phi-Genesis results. Past target dates are historical planning targets, not current delivery promises.

docs.title: 1. Mission
docs.text:
Build a deterministic, mathematically verified economic layer for distributed systems where invariants are hard constraints enforced at every state transition.

Core principle: Correctness is not assumed — it is measured, fuzzed, and documented. Every state transition must satisfy the SIRM invariant suite (I1–I4) or be explicitly rejected.

docs.title: 2. Strategic priority: mathematics and evidence first
docs.text: This is a reading order and research map, not a theorem asserting that each downstream application follows from the mathematics. The fourth-moment theorem does not prove the SIRM invariants, the higher-moment recurrence, the Phi-Genesis decimation mechanism, or a quantum advantage. The separate RFT-Cosmology-Genesis repository now records an exact algebraic limit and finite-level remainder for its defined normalized invariant; its cosmological extension remains phenomenological and has no full observational-likelihood validation.

docs.title: Priority I — protect and independently audit the formal theorem
docs.text:
Primary source: Evgeny-Theorem · Lean formalization · theorem statement.

For the specific operator definitions and assumptions in the source repository, the fourth-moment trace defect is stated as

\[ \Delta_m(H^4,\theta) = \mathrm{Tr}(H_C^4)-\mathrm{Tr}(H_{C'}^4) = -16(3^{m-1}+1)\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad m\ge 1. \]

With the documented normalization,

\[ I_m(\theta) = \frac{\Delta_m(H^4,\theta)}{3^{m+1}+3} \longrightarrow -\frac{16}{9}\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right), \qquad I_m\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\longrightarrow-\frac{8}{9}. \]

docs.title: Closure and maintenance tasks
docs.text:
• Keep the theorem statement, operator definitions, and normalization synchronized with the primary repository; treat that repository as authoritative.
  • Re-run the Lean build from the documented formalization directory after any theorem or dependency change, and report the exact command and result.
  • Independently check the finite-level trace identity against the stated formula, including the boundary cases and the angle convention.
  • Keep the fourth-moment result separate from the higher-moment recurrence: do not describe the all-level recurrence as proved unless its proof is present and verified.
  • Track numerical or spectral-decimation observations as separate evidence; they do not replace the formal theorem's assumptions or proof.

docs.title: Priority II — maintain the higher-moment proof hierarchy
docs.text: Keep the proof status moment-specific: H⁶ and H⁸ have Lean recurrences for \(m\ge3\) plus exact finite \(m=2\to3\) certificates; H¹⁰ has an unconditional Lean recurrence for \(m\ge4\) and affine form for \(m\ge5\). Continue the derivation of a unified general recurrence without promoting finite certificates or one moment's theorem to a universal result.

docs.title: Priority III — extend the proved Phi-Genesis spectral results and audit Gate A separately
docs.text:
Phi-Genesis now has two distinct machine-checked results:

  1. Uniform lower bound: every real eigenvalue with a nonzero real eigenvector of the explicitly defined signed Laplacian is at least \(1\), at every refinement level.
  2. Least-eigenvalue convergence: for the signless graph matrices \(Q_{6+n}\) and their gauge-conjugate signed matrices, the least eigenvalues converge to \(\lambda_\infty\). The exact enclosure is
\[ \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810187}{10^{36}} \le\lambda_\infty\le \frac{1309128920280813421888623088170810189}{10^{36}}. \]

Thus \(\lambda_\infty\approx1.309128920280813421888623088170810188\), with interval width \(2\times10^{-36}\). The convergence statement covers levels \(N\ge6\). This is a graph-spectral limit, not a known fundamental physical constant.

Preserve these as completed results within their exact matrix and level scopes. Continue the separate work on Gate A's exceptional set, the quadratic increment law, a closed form for the limit, levels \(N<6\), and the external \(\theta=2\pi\) identification. Do not describe the whole spectral-decimation mechanism as closed.

docs.title: Priority IV — specify and verify SIRM as an engineering model
docs.text:
SIRM uses four stated runtime constraints. Short symbols are used below to keep the equations robust across GitHub Markdown renderers; the table maps each symbol to the implementation variable.

\[ \begin{aligned} I_1:\quad & S = B + Gp,\\ I_2:\quad & S = M - D,\\ I_3:\quad & d < p \quad (p>0),\\ I_4:\quad & E_i \ge -\frac{S}{10p}. \end{aligned} \]

The effective-balance relation is

\[ E_i = b_i + G. \] Symbol Implementation variable \(S\) total_supply \(B\) total_base_sum \(G\) global_field \(M\) total_minted \(D\) total_burned \(d\) dust_accumulator \(E_i\) effective_balance[i] \(b_i\) base_balance[i]

These constraints are an engineering specification; they are not consequences of the fourth-moment theorem.

docs.title: Priority V — evaluate applications against their own evidence

Assess Rift-L1, Rift-Network, scheduler, memory-context, and exploratory application tracks using their own tests, audits, benchmarks, and deployment criteria. Do not infer production readiness or quantum advantage from the mathematical results above.
3. The RFT Methodology
docs.text:
RFT-SIRM operates as a multi-stage research pipeline. Each stage feeds into the next, but stages are independent enough to be evaluated, funded, and deployed separately.

┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│   Stage 0       │ --> │   Stage 1       │ --> │   Stage 2       │
│  Mathematical   │     │  Reference      │     │  Protocol       │
│  Foundation     │     │  Implementation │     │  Deployment     │
│  (SIRM)         │     │  (Rust/Anchor)  │     │  (Solana L1)    │
└─────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘

Key insight: Stages are decoupled. SIRM can be instantiated in any runtime — Solana, standalone L1, or future environments — without changing the invariant specification.
